thread.title: Market slides as tech bears take a bite out of FAANG stocks

author: Cromwell Schubarth
title: Market slides as tech bears take a bite out of FAANG stocks
text: – TechFlash Editor, Silicon Valley Business Journal Nov 19, 2018, 3:05pm PST Updated Nov 19, 2018, 3:27pm PST For the first time in seven years, all five tech companies that make up the so-called FAANG stocks — Facebook, Apple, Amazon.com, Netflix and Google — dropped into bear market territory on Monday. Both Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL) and Google parent Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) finished Monday at prices that are 20 percent below their record highs of earlier this year, which is the definition of a bear drop in their values. Apple finished trading on Monday down nearly 4 percent at $185.86. Its shares slid after another report on Monday that said the company was cutting supplier orders related to its new iPhone models amid unexpectedly tepid demand. Google parent Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) finished the day down by nearly 4 percent at $1,027.42. The other three components of the FANG group of tech stocks — Facebook Inc., Netflix Inc. and Amazon Inc. — were already in bear market territory before Monday's closing prices. Facebook, which has been pummeled by scandals around data privacy and executive ethics this year, is now about 40 percent below its record high. The stock (NASDAQ:FB) finished Monday down by nearly 6 percent at $131.55. Netflix (NASDAQ:NFLX) dropped by more than 5 percent to $270.60 on Monday and is now down about 36 percent. Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) fell another 5.1 percent on Monday to close at $1,512.29 and is now down by about 26 percent since its high. Overall, the Nasdaq Composite Index was down by about 3 percent Monday and is about 12 percent below its 52-week high. The S&P 500 Index dropped between 1 percent and 2 percent on Monday and is down by about 8.5 percent from it 52-week high. Collectively, the market caps of the FAANG companies are down more than $1 trillion, meaning they've erased as much market value in recent weeks as the two largest companies, Apple and Amazon, were each worth until recently. The broader tech selloff swept up smaller Silicon Valley stocks Monday as well. The 10 other largest decliners among the region's stocks were: Zuora Inc.
